chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Oaths are of three types: an oath with no expiation, an oath with an expiation, and a swamping oath that necessitates Hellfire. As for the oath with no expiation, it is when a man swears not to do an act of piety, and its expiation is that he does it. And the oath upon which expiation is obligatory is when a man swears not to commit a sin, but he does it, so expiation becomes obligatory for him regarding it. And the swamping oath that necessitates Hellfire is when a man swears regarding the right of a Muslim, specifically regarding the withholding of his property.

key_terms.يَمِينٌ غَمُوسٌ: Swamping oath (an oath that 'drowns' the person in sin/Hellfire)

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of oaths in Shia jurisprudence and their respective expiations?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi categorizes oaths into three legal types: 'non-expiatory' oaths of piety where fulfilling the act serves as expiation, 'expiatory' oaths of sin requiring standard kaffarah upon fulfillment, and 'swallowing' (ghamūs) oaths involving the rights of others, which incur Hellfire. This classification highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that the nature of the oath's content—whether it pertains to voluntary piety, obligatory sin, or specific rights (haqq)—determines the spiritual and legal consequence, emphasizing the protection of individual rights in oath-making.
